newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CLINTON TO ADDRESS JOINT SITTING IN AUSTRALIA
The Prime Minister says US President Bill Clinton will address all Federal Parliamentarians in the House of Representatives next month.
President Clinton visits Australia from November the 19th to the 23rd.
Senate President Margaret Reid argued it would be more appropriate for him to give an address in the Great Hall in Parliament House.
But Mr Howard says President Clinton will address a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament, in the House of Representatives, as President George Bush did in 1991.
Mr Howard says President Clinton's visit to Australia will be widely welcomed by the Australian community.
SECOND SKIN GRAFT FOR CAIRNS BOY
The six-year-old boy who was burnt in a Cairns school yard last week will undergo a second skin graft operation today.
Surgeons will graft artificial skin to the back of six-year-old Tjandamurra O'Shane .
He'll then return to the intensive care unit at the Royal Children's Hospital.
Doctors say his condition remains serious, but stable.
A 26-year-old man has been charged with having unlawfully attempted to kill the boy.
SCHOOL SECURITY REVIEW AFTER CAIRNS TRAGEDY
Queensland's Education Minister says he hopes to have a report by Christmas on ways to improve school security, following an attack on a Cairns boy last week.
Bob Quinn ordered a review of school security, after the attack on six year old Tjandamurra O'Shane who was doused with petrol and set alight in the grounds of the Cairns North State School.
Mr Quinn all stakeholders, including parents and teachers will be involved in the process.
He says, however, that there won't ever be a one hundred percent guarantee of school security.
800 JOBS SAVED IN CANBERRA TAX OFFICE
Pressure from staff, the community and politicians has saved 800 jobs in the Canberra Tax Office.
The office says it has reconsidered its original plan to make the cuts, after getting negative feedback about the move.
One M-P who lobbied against the planned cuts, John Langmore, says the loss of 800 jobs would have been devistating to the Canberra community.
Mr Langmore says its a great victory for those who's positions are now safe.
